questionText:
Read the following excerpt on the Swadeshi art movement and the genesis of the Bengal School and answer the questions:

The Bengal School of Painting emerged in the first decade of the 20th century as the powerful visual wing of the anti-partition Swadeshi movement. Led by Ernest Binfield (E.B.) Havell, the visionary Principal of the Government School of Art, Calcutta, and Abanindranath Tagore, who became Vice-Principal in 1905, the movement launched a radical aesthetic rebellion against Western academic realism. Havell took the controversial step of removing European plaster casts from the school and exhibiting Mughal, Rajput, and Ajanta masterpieces, urging Indian students to draw spiritual inspiration from their own civilizational heritage. Supported by Sister Nivedita, Ananda K. Coomaraswamy, and Japanese philosopher Kakuzo Okakura (who proclaimed 'Asia is One'), Abanindranath synthesized indigenous miniature traditions with Japanese wash techniques to create a poetic, dream-like national visual language that restored cultural pride and laid the foundation for modern Indian art.

The Swadeshi Movement protesting the Partition of Bengal

The Bengal School was the visual embodiment of the 1905 Swadeshi movement, asserting cultural nationalism through art.
Hence Option A is correct.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

When the Constituent Assembly of India completed drafting the Constitution of the Republic of India, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru personally invited Nandalal Bose and his master students from Kala Bhavana, Santiniketan, to illustrate the original calligraphed manuscript. Working between 1949 and 1950, Nandalal executed 22 monumental header panels for the 22 parts of the Constitution, visually chronicling 5,000 years of Indian civilizational history. Each illustration was carefully chosen to reflect the spirit of the corresponding constitutional text: Part III on Fundamental Rights is headed by Lord Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana returning victoriously to Ayodhya; Part IV on Directive Principles of State Policy depicts Lord Krishna preaching the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna on the battlefield; and other sections feature seals from the Indus Valley Civilization, the Vedic ashram, Gautam Buddha, Lord Mahavira, Emperor Ashoka, Emperor Akbar, Chhatrapati Shivaji, Rani Lakshmibai, Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi March, and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.

questionText:

Statement I: Jamini Roy deliberately rejected his formal British academic training and Bengal wash style to embrace the raw, earthy folk idiom of Bengal village patuas.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Statement I is correct: Jamini Roy abandoned academic realism and wash painting to revive folk art. Statement II is incorrect: he completely discarded Western oil paints, formulating his own natural earth pigments applied in flat gouache/tempera.
Hence Option B is correct.
Hence, option (C) is correct.
